-accesscode.what: Steam UI (steamui.so) switch, probably supplying an access/activation code at startup; the related `-accesscode=` form is forwarded by the client's command-line handler alongside `-login`/`-applaunch`, so it likely takes `-accesscode=<code>`. Purpose not confirmed.

-all_languages.what: VGUI localization (vgui2_s.so) flag: load localization files for all languages instead of only the current `%language%` one, probably for translation testing. Presence flag.

-allosarches.what: Bootstrapper flag: request client packages for every OS architecture rather than only the running one, typically for mirroring or testing the package manifest. Presence flag.

-allosvers.what: Bootstrapper flag: request client packages for every OS version in the manifest, not just the current one. Presence flag; pairs with `-allosarches`.

-allowbrowserviewunderlays.what: steamwebhelper flag (Valve: allow browser view underlays). It is the webhelper-side counterpart of `-cef-allow-browser-underlays`, which steamclient passes through when launching the webhelper.

-allowremotediscovery.what: steamclient.so flag for the Remote Play / In-Home Streaming client manager: probably allows this client to be discovered by, or to discover, remote Steam clients. It sits next to the opposite switch `-preventsteamdiscovery`.

-alwaysrelaunch.what: Bootstrapper flag: always re-exec the client after the update step, even when nothing changed. Presence flag.

-applaunch.what: Launch a game when Steam starts: `steam -applaunch <appid> [game args...]`. It is handled by the Steam UI command-line dispatcher (CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine) and also forwarded to an already running instance.

-arch.what: Registered in steamclient/chromehtml next to the CEF switches, and the bootstrapper uses it to request packages for a given architecture. Probably takes an architecture value such as `-arch x64`; the client also appends `&ARCH=%s` to the Steam UI URL.

-batterytestmode.help: rapidly cycle battery percentages for testing
-batterytestmode.what: Test hook in the steamclient system manager. It makes the reported battery percentage cycle rapidly instead of reading SDL_GetPowerInfo, so the battery UI can be exercised on Deck-style devices.

-bigpicture.help: Start in Steam Big Picture mode
-bigpicture.what: Start the client directly in Big Picture mode (steamui.so). Related switches: `-tenfoot` (alias), `-gamepadui` and `-nobigpicture` (force off).

-bootreserve.what: steamclient.so flag, probably reserving a block of disk space at boot as a safety buffer (sized by `-bootreservesizemb`). Evidence is only adjacent strings.

-bootreservesizemb.what: steamclient.so switch that probably takes a size in MB for the `-bootreserve` reservation (`-bootreservesizemb <MB>`). Evidence is only the name.

-bootstrapperproxy.what: Bootstrapper switch that takes an argument: an HTTP proxy used for the bootstrapper's own package downloads.

-buildid.what: steamsysinfo option: `-buildid <id>`, the build identifier attached to crash reports. It is used together with `-steamid`, `-logdir`, `-query` and `-out-file`.

-cafeapplaunch.help: Launch apps in a cyber cafe context
-cafeapplaunch.what: steamclient.so switch: launch apps in a cyber-cafe (internet cafe licensing) context. Presence flag.

-candidates.help: Show libjingle candidates for local connection as they are processed
-candidates.what: steamclient.so debug flag: log the libjingle ICE candidates for local P2P/streaming connections as they are processed.

-ccsyntax.help: Spew details about the localized strings we load
-ccsyntax.what: VGUI localization debug flag: log details about each localized string file and token that is loaded. Useful together with `-language`.

-cef-allow-browser-underlays.help: Allow webhelper to create BrowserView underlays
-cef-allow-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: allow steamwebhelper to create BrowserView underlays. steamclient forwards it to the webhelper as `-allowbrowserviewunderlays`.

-cef-disable-breakpad.what: CEF switch: disable Breakpad crash reporting in steamwebhelper.

-cef-disable-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: turn off BrowserView underlay support in steamwebhelper. It is the opposite of `-cef-force-browser-underlays`.

-cef-disable-gpu.help: Disable GPU usage in CEF (force software rendering/compositing)
-cef-disable-gpu.what: CEF switch: disable GPU use in steamwebhelper, forcing software rendering and compositing. This is a common workaround for black or flickering Steam windows caused by driver problems.

-cef-disable-gpu-compositing.help: Disable GPU accelerated compositing in browsers
-cef-disable-gpu-compositing.what: CEF switch: disable GPU-accelerated compositing in steamwebhelper while other GPU use stays enabled.

-cef-disable-gpu-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable the Chromium GPU-process sandbox in steamwebhelper.

-cef-disable-hang-timeouts.help: disables GPU and renderer hang timeouts
-cef-disable-hang-timeouts.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium's GPU and renderer hang watchdogs, so a stalled webhelper process isn't killed. Useful when debugging the webhelper.

-cef-disable-hevc.what: CEF switch: disable HEVC (H.265) video support in steamwebhelper.

-cef-disable-js-logging.help: disables console and log file logging of JS console events
-cef-disable-js-logging.what: CEF switch: stop logging Steam UI JavaScript console messages to the console and to the webhelper log file.

-cef-disable-logging.what: CEF switch: disable CEF/Chromium logging from steamwebhelper.

-cef-disable-occlusion.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium's window-occlusion detection, so hidden or covered Steam windows keep rendering.

-cef-disable-renderer-restart.help: Disable auto-restart of renderer process for existing browsers
-cef-disable-renderer-restart.what: CEF switch: don't automatically restart a crashed renderer process for an existing browser.

-cef-disable-safe-shutdown-workaround.help: Disable the usage of the safe browser shutdown workaround for Linux+NV
-cef-disable-safe-shutdown-workaround.what: CEF switch: turn off the safe browser shutdown workaround that is otherwise applied on Linux with NVIDIA drivers. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-disable_safe_shutdown_workaround`; the env var `STEAM_DISABLE_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_WORKAROUND` has the same effect.

-cef-disable-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium sandboxing in steamwebhelper. `-no-cef-sandbox` is registered next to it as an equivalent.

-cef-disable-seccomp-sandbox.help: disables CEF seccomp-bpf sandbox on Linux
-cef-disable-seccomp-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable only the Linux seccomp-bpf layer of the Chromium sandbox.

-cef-disable-site-isolation.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium per-site process isolation, which reduces the number of renderer processes.

-cef-disable-touch-focus-workaround.help: Disable touch input browser focus workaround
-cef-disable-touch-focus-workaround.what: CEF switch: turn off the touch-input browser-focus workaround. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-disabletouchfocusworkaround`.

-cef-disable-xcomposite-workaround.help: Disable the glcomposer workaround applied to some video drivers
-cef-disable-xcomposite-workaround.what: CEF switch: turn off the glcomposer/XComposite workaround that is applied automatically for some video drivers.

-cef-enable-debugging.help: enables Chromium remote debugging, defaulting to localhost:8080
-cef-enable-debugging.what: CEF switch: enable Chromium remote debugging (DevTools protocol) on localhost:8080 by default; the port can be changed with `-devtools-port`. Afterwards you can attach Chrome DevTools to the Steam UI.

-cef-enable-gpu-debugging.help: Enable GPU debugging in Chromium, costs a glGetError() call after every command
-cef-enable-gpu-debugging.what: CEF switch: enable Chromium GPU debugging, which runs glGetError() after every GL command. It is very slow.

-cef-enable-low-delay-live-stream.help: Reduce buffering requirements for live video playback
-cef-enable-low-delay-live-stream.what: CEF switch: reduce buffering for live video playback (e.g. Steam Broadcasts) in the webhelper.

-cef-enable-vaapi.help: Enable VA-API video decoding on Linux
-cef-enable-vaapi.what: CEF switch: enable VA-API hardware video decoding in steamwebhelper on Linux.

-cef-force-accessibility.what: CEF switch: force-enable Chromium accessibility. The webhelper is then started with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, for screen readers.

-cef-force-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: force BrowserView underlays on even where they are off by default. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-forcebrowserviewunderlays`.

-cef-force-gpu.what: CEF switch: force GPU acceleration in steamwebhelper even where it would be disabled (e.g. by the blocklist).

-cef-force-gpu-blocklist.what: CEF switch: force Chromium's GPU driver blocklist on, so blocklisted GPUs fall back to software.

-cef-force-hw-video-decode.help: Force enable HW accelerated video decoding
-cef-force-hw-video-decode.what: CEF switch: force hardware-accelerated video decoding in steamwebhelper.

-cef-force-occlusion.help: force enable Chromium window occlusion testing
-cef-force-occlusion.what: CEF switch: force Chromium window-occlusion detection on. It is the opposite of `-cef-disable-occlusion`.

-cef-force-opaque-backgrounds.help: Force the usage of opaque backgrounds for CEF
-cef-force-opaque-backgrounds.what: CEF switch: force opaque, non-transparent backgrounds for CEF browsers. Possibly a workaround for compositors that render transparency badly.

-cef-force-sandbox.what: CEF switch: force the Chromium sandbox on even where Steam would disable it.

-cef-full-memory-crash-report.what: CEF switch: write full-memory crash dumps for steamwebhelper crashes instead of minidumps.

-cef-log-sandbox.what: CEF switch: enable logging of Chromium sandbox decisions in steamwebhelper.

-cef-use-vulkan.what: CEF switch: run Chromium's ANGLE graphics layer on its Vulkan backend instead of the default GL backend.

-cef-verbose-js-logging.help: enables verbose logging of JS console events
-cef-verbose-js-logging.what: CEF switch: log Steam UI JavaScript console events verbosely. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-verbosejslogging`.

-cef-verbose-logging.what: CEF switch: enable verbose Chromium/CEF logging in steamwebhelper.

-cef-verbose-modules.help: enables verbose logging for specific CEF modules
-cef-verbose-modules.what: CEF switch: enable verbose logging for selected CEF modules. It probably takes a module list in Chromium `--vmodule` style; the format is not confirmed.

-child-update-ui.what: Internal bootstrapper flag: marks a process as the forked child that draws the update/progress UI. It is not meant to be passed by hand.

-child-update-ui-socket.what: Internal bootstrapper switch: `-child-update-ui-socket <fd>` gives the update-UI child the IPC socket for talking to the parent bootstrapper.

-chromeos.what: ChromeOS (Borealis) integration flag read by tier0 platform detection. It makes Steam behave as the ChromeOS build.

-chromeosverbose.what: ChromeOS (Borealis) verbose flag: more logging for ChromeOS-specific paths, such as the disk-space management that calls `/usr/bin/crosdisk` (BEnsureDiskSpaceAvailable / BReleaseExcessDiskSpace).

-clearbeta.what: Bootstrapper flag: leave the client beta and return to the stable branch by removing `package/beta`. Platform-specific branch prefixes (`steamdeck_`, `steampal_`, `chromeos_`) are handled near it.

-clientbeta.help: Overrides Steam client beta for single session
-clientbeta.what: `-clientbeta <branch>`: run a different client beta branch for this session only, without changing the saved `package/beta`. The log says "Overriding client beta for this session ... (clientbeta flag)".

-compat.what: VGUI flag, probably a compatibility mode for UI DPI scaling (it sits next to the `DPIScaling` registry value and `-nodpiscale`).

-compat-disable-filtering.help: Disable filtering of normally unlisted runtimes.
-compat-disable-filtering.what: Steam Play/compat tools switch: show compatibility tools/runtimes that are normally hidden (unlisted) in the selection UI.

-compat-force-slr.help: Force enable/disable using SLR 1.0 by default over legacy LD_* setup.
-compat-force-slr.what: Steam Play switch: force the Steam Linux Runtime 1.0 (scout) container on or off by default for native Linux games, instead of the legacy LD_* library-path setup. Probably takes a 0/1 value.

-complete_install_via_http.help: Run installation completion over HTTP by default
-complete_install_via_http.what: steamclient.so switch: run install-completion steps over HTTP by default instead of the CM connection. Presence flag.

-console.what: Steam UI flag: enable the developer console in the client (Console tab / `steam://open/console`), where the concommands documented here are typed. `-noconsole` is the opposite.

-controllertypeoverride.what: steamclient.so controller switch that probably takes a controller type value and overrides the detected controller type. It sits next to `-forcedeckcontroller` and haptic convars.

-debug_steamapi.help: enables logging of Steam API functions
-debug_steamapi.what: steamclient.so switch: log Steam API (steamworks interface) calls made by games. Output probably goes to the `apiwarning_log`/steam_api log.

-debugamf.help: Enable AMF video encoding debug log
-debugamf.what: Steam UI switch: enable AMD AMF video-encoder debug logging. This affects Remote Play and game recording encode paths.

-debugbreak.what: Low-level (tier0) debug flag read by the bootstrapper, crashhandler, steamservice and others: trigger a debugger break at startup so a debugger can attach. Presence flag.

-debugoutputlogs.what: Mirror log output to the debug output/console as well as the log files. It is read by the bootstrapper, client, overlay and webhelper; `log_files_always_flush` and `STEAM_CLIENT_LOG_FOLDER` sit next to it.

-deckard.what: tier0 platform flag named after the hardware codename Deckard (related to `-steamframe`). It makes the client behave as that device. Exact effect unknown.

-delaypageload.what: steamwebhelper switch, probably delaying the initial page load in the webhelper (e.g. to give time to attach a debugger). Evidence is only the name.

-dev.what: Developer mode: enables developer log output and dev features across the bootstrapper, client, UI and overlay. Examples are extra HTML context-menu items (View Source, Open DevTools, Inspect Element), the WebUI transport server-status endpoint, and devkit controller hooks.

-devsites.what: Point the client's web pages (store, community, etc.) at Valve's local development websites instead of production. Used together with `-devsiteshost`.

-devsiteshost.help: Pass the hostname, will generate dev site domains like store.{hostname}.steam.dev
-devsiteshost.what: `-devsiteshost <hostname>`: build dev site domains such as `store.<hostname>.steam.dev` for `-devsites`. This is Valve-internal.

-devtools-port.what: `-devtools-port <port>`: sets the Chromium remote-debugging port of steamwebhelper (passed as `--remote-debugging-port=%s`, bound to 127.0.0.1 with `--remote-allow-origins=*`). The default is 8080. Use it with `-cef-enable-debugging`.

-disable-libusb.help: Disable support for controllers requiring exclusive USB access
-disable-libusb.what: Disable the steamclient controller support for devices that need exclusive USB (libusb) access. It is the opposite of `-enable-libusb`.

-disable-overlay-gpu-pri.help: Disables setting webhelper GPU pri high when overlay visible
-disable-overlay-gpu-pri.what: Overlay switch: don't raise steamwebhelper's GPU scheduling priority while the in-game overlay is visible. The delay between priority changes is set by `-overlay-gpu-pri-delay`.

-disable-overlay-wait-for-cef-frame.help: Disables waiting for pending CEF frame render when overlay visible.
-disable-overlay-wait-for-cef-frame.what: Overlay switch: don't wait for a pending CEF frame to finish rendering before presenting while the overlay is visible. Possibly reduces stalls at the cost of stale or partial overlay frames.

-disable-winh264.what: Windows-only CEF switch: don't load winh264.dll for H.264 decoding. It has no effect on Linux.

-disable_broadcast_webrtc.what: steamclient.so flag: disable the WebRTC transport for Steam Broadcasting sessions (`Broadcast.BeginBroadcastSession`). Presence flag.

-disable_safe_shutdown_workaround.what: steamwebhelper flag: skip the safe browser shutdown workaround (logs "Skipping safe browser shutdown workaround: disabled"). Same as setting `STEAM_DISABLE_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_WORKAROUND`; the client sets it from `-cef-disable-safe-shutdown-workaround`.

-disablehighdpi.what: CEF switch: disable high-DPI scaling support in steamwebhelper.

-disablejslogging.help: disable file and console logging of JS console events
-disablejslogging.what: steamwebhelper switch: disable file and console logging of JS console events. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-js-logging`.

-disablelauncherservice.what: steamclient.so switch: don't start the `steam-runtime-launcher-service` helper process. That process lets commands be run inside a game's pressure-vessel container for debugging.

-disablepartnerlicenses.help: disable automatically granted partner licenses - impacts all web and client sessions, don't try to use with multiple active steam clients!
-disablepartnerlicenses.what: Valve/partner dev switch: disable automatically granted partner licenses. Valve warns that this affects all web and client sessions of the account, so don't use it with several active clients.

-disablerendererrestart.help: disable auto-restarting a renderer for an existing browser
-disablerendererrestart.what: steamwebhelper switch: don't auto-restart a crashed renderer for an existing browser. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-renderer-restart`.

-disabletouchfocusworkaround.help: disable touch input browser focus workaround
-disabletouchfocusworkaround.what: steamwebhelper switch: disable the touch-input focus workaround. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-touch-focus-workaround`.

-disablevulkanlayer.help: Prevents loading of Vulkan layer if overlay disabled
-disablevulkanlayer.what: Overlay switch: when the overlay is disabled, also stop loading Steam's Vulkan overlay layer into games.

-display-scale=.what: VGUI (legacy UI) switch `-display-scale=<factor>`: overrides the X11 display scale factor, which otherwise comes from things like `GDK_SCALE`. The format is assumed numeric.

-download.what: Bootstrapper flag: download the client package set only, probably without installing or launching. The related strings are about package download and metrics caching.

-drop.what: Steam UI command-line verb handled by CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine together with `-applaunch`/`-install`. It probably means drag-and-drop or dropped-file handling; the meaning is unclear.

-dumpvideostream.help: Dump the game stream as an elementary video file
-dumpvideostream.what: Remote Play debug switch: write the received game stream to disk as an elementary (raw H.264/HEVC) video file.

-enable-desktop-gl-fallback.what: Steam UI switch, probably allowing a fallback to desktop OpenGL for UI rendering when the preferred path fails. It sits next to `-opengl`/`-fullscreenopengl`.

-enable-devkit.what: Enable Steam devkit features in the client: the devkit service used for SteamOS/Deck game development, and app-management console commands such as `app_install`.

-enable-keyring.help: enables CEF usage of the Chromium keyring
-enable-keyring.what: CEF switch: let steamwebhelper use the Chromium/OS keyring (e.g. GNOME Keyring/KWallet) for stored secrets instead of basic storage.

-enable-libusb.help: Enable support for controllers requiring exclusive USB access
-enable-libusb.what: Enable steamclient controller support for devices that need exclusive USB (libusb) access, instead of the kernel/hidraw path.

-enable-libusb-gamecube.help: Enable support for Nintendo GameCube adapters in Wii-U mode
-enable-libusb-gamecube.what: Enable support for the Nintendo GameCube controller adapter in Wii U mode through libusb.

-exitsteam.what: Ask an already running Steam to exit. The bootstrapper forwards the command line to the running instance and the Steam UI handles it in CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine. Comparable to `-shutdown`.

-failsystemcheck.what: Bootstrapper test hook: make the system requirements check fail on purpose, to test the failure dialog.

-flushconfig.what: Steam UI flag, probably resetting or flushing local client configuration (for example cached UI/dialog config) at startup, much like Steam's old `steam://flushconfig`. Exact scope unconfirmed.

-force-no-dbus-simulate-user-activity.what: Client/UI flag: never call the D-Bus 'simulate user activity' (screensaver inhibit / wake) method, probably for desktops where it misbehaves.

-force-oobe-stage1.what: Force the first stage of the out-of-box experience (first-boot setup on Steam Deck/SteamOS) to show.

-force-oobe-stage2.what: Force the second stage of the out-of-box experience (post-login setup on SteamOS/Deck) to show.

-forcebrowserviewunderlays.what: steamwebhelper switch: force browser view underlays on. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-force-browser-underlays`.

-forcecontrollerappid.help: Force a Specific AppID for Steam Controller Config - Prevents context/app switching from changing configuration
-forcecontrollerappid.what: `-forcecontrollerappid <appid>`: lock Steam Input to the controller configuration of the given app, so switching apps or context doesn't change the active config. Used for testing controller configs.

-forcedeckcontroller.what: steamclient.so flag: treat the built-in controller as a Steam Deck controller, as when running on a Deck (registry markers `IsSteamDeck`). Mainly for emulating Deck input.

-forceguiupdater.what: Bootstrapper flag: always use the graphical update/progress window rather than the text UI.

-forcemanifestsuffix.what: Bootstrapper switch that takes an argument: override the client manifest filename suffix (`steam_client_<suffix>`) to fetch a different manifest.

-forcepackagedownload.what: Bootstrapper flag: re-download the client package zips even if the cached ones look valid.

-forcesteamupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: force a client update check and apply the result at startup.

-forceunsupportedos.what: Bootstrapper flag: keep running on an OS that the manifest marks as unsupported.

-foreground.what: Steam UI command-line verb: bring the existing Steam window to the foreground. It is usually forwarded to the running instance.

-friendsui.what: Force-load the friends UI module (friendsui.so) in the client, UI and overlay. `-nofriendsui` is the opposite.

-fs_log.what: Filesystem (filesystem_stdio) switch: log file-system accesses made by the client.

-fs_logbins.help: Log the binaries we load during operation
-fs_logbins.what: Filesystem switch: log every binary/shared library loaded while running.

-fs_target.what: Filesystem switch (Valve: "Set target syntax"): probably takes a value selecting the path/target syntax used by `-fs_log` output. Format unknown.

-full_memory_dump.what: Bootstrapper/crash-handler flag: write full memory dumps instead of minidumps on a crash. The related env var is `BREAKPAD_DUMP_LOCATION`.

-fullscreen.what: Start Big Picture mode fullscreen. `-windowed` is the windowed counterpart.

-fullscreenopengl.help: Use the full screen OpenGL render for the UI
-fullscreenopengl.what: Legacy VGUI switch: use the full-screen OpenGL renderer for the UI. Probably a leftover from the old Big Picture.

-gameid.what: Overlay (gameoverlayui) flag, probably `-gameid <gameid>`, telling the overlay process which game it is attached to. It is set by the client, not by users.

-gameidlaunch.what: Steam UI command-line verb: launch a game by its 64-bit game ID (which covers mods and shortcuts), e.g. `-gameidlaunch <gameid>`. Compare `-applaunch`, which takes an app ID.

-gameinput.help: Use Microsoft GameInput for controller support
-gameinput.what: Use Microsoft GameInput for controller input. This is Windows-only and does nothing on Linux.

-gamepadui.what: Start in the gamepad UI (the Steam Deck / new Big Picture interface). On SteamOS it is used together with `-steamdeck`/`-steamos3`.

-hardware-updater.what: Steam UI flag: force-enable the hardware (controller/device firmware) updater. `-no-hardware-updater` is the opposite.

-holo.what: tier0 platform flag for SteamOS 3 (codename holo). It is treated the same as `-steamos3`.

-hometest.what: Steam UI flag that exercises the hardware survey scheduling (SurveyDate, SurveyDateVersion, SurveyDateSteamDeckDelay) next to `-steamconsole`. Probably forces or tests the survey prompt; the effect is unclear.

-html-enable-tooltips.what: Show native browser tooltips (HTML `title` attributes) in the client's HTML surfaces.

-html-perf-monitor.what: Draw an HTML performance overlay (frame timing data) on webhelper-rendered surfaces in the client and overlay.

-ifrunning.what: Bootstrapper/UI flag: only act (forward the command line, e.g. a `steam://` URL) if Steam is already running; don't start a new client otherwise.

-inhibitbootstrap.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the bootstrap/update step and start whatever client is installed. Same effect as `BootStrapperInhibitAll` in steam.cfg.

-init_universe.what: steamclient.so switch, probably `-init_universe <universe>`, which picks the Steam universe (public/beta/dev) at startup. Valve-internal.

-install.what: Steam UI command-line verb: start installing an app, probably `-install <appid>` (compare `-uninstall`). It is forwarded to the running instance.

-installupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: apply a pending client update that was already downloaded ("Found pending update", "Applying update...").

-language.what: `-language <name>`: sets the client UI language for this run, e.g. `-language german` or `schinese`. It also chooses the bootstrapper's `steambootstrapper_<lang>.txt` strings.

-led-enumerate-sysfs-all.what: Steam UI (device LED control) switch: list all LED devices under sysfs, not only the ones Steam recognises. `-testled` creates a fake LED for testing.

-log_voice.help: writes voice chat data to the logs/voice_log.txt file
-log_voice.what: Write voice chat data to `logs/voice_log.txt` for debugging.

-logdir.what: steamsysinfo option `-logdir <dir>`: the directory where the system-info tool writes its logs.

-login.what: Automatically log in a user: `-login <username> [password]`. With credentials on the command line, `-rememberpassword` acts as if 'remember my password' was ticked.

-lognetapi.help: logs all P2P networking info to log/netapi_log.txt
-lognetapi.what: Log all P2P networking (ISteamNetworking) activity to `logs/netapi_log.txt`.

-longestloc.help: Use longest string for each localization token
-longestloc.what: Localization test switch: for each token, use the longest translation across all languages, so UI layouts can be checked for text overflow.

-ltp.what: steamclient.so switch: use the legacy scheme for storing the login refresh token (JWT) on disk, e.g. under `Software\Valve\Steam\ConnectCache` in registry.vdf.

-manuallyclearframes.help: Should the overlay be manually clearing frames to black (because the game doesn't clear the entire screen?)
-manuallyclearframes.what: gameoverlayui switch: make the overlay clear its frames to black itself, for games that don't clear the whole screen and would otherwise leave artifacts.

-master_ipc_name_override.what: `-master_ipc_name_override <name>`: overrides the name of the master IPC/shared-memory channel used between the bootstrapper, client and UI. With a different name, a second, separate Steam instance can run (developer use).

-net_fake_state.what: `-net_fake_state <state>`: sets the initial value of the `net_fake_state` convar, which simulates network conditions. Valid states: normal, NoLAN, CaptivePortal_Redirected, CaptivePortal_InPlace, NoInternet, NoSteam.

-net_start_wifi_disabled.help: Set the initial value for wifi enabled to false.  (Useful when emulating SteamDeck)
-net_start_wifi_disabled.what: Start with Wi-Fi reported as disabled. Valve says this is useful when emulating a Steam Deck on a desktop.

-no-cef-sandbox.what: Disable the Chromium sandbox in steamwebhelper; same effect as `-cef-disable-sandbox`. Useful on systems without unprivileged user namespaces.

-no-child-update-ui.what: Bootstrapper flag: draw the update UI in the bootstrapper process itself instead of a forked `-child-update-ui` process.

-no-dwrite.help: forces vgui to use GDI text even if DWrite support is available
-no-dwrite.what: Windows-only: make VGUI use GDI text instead of DirectWrite. It has no effect on Linux.

-no-hardware-updater.what: Steam UI flag: disable the hardware/firmware updater (controller and device firmware update prompts). `-hardware-updater` is the opposite.

-no-shared-textures.help: forces overlay to avoid sharing texture handles with game process
-no-shared-textures.what: Overlay switch: don't share GPU texture handles between the overlay and the game process; the overlay uses a copy path instead. Can work around overlay glitches with some drivers.

-noassert.what: tier0 flag read by the bootstrapper, crashhandler and helpers: don't break or show dialogs on (non-fatal) asserts. Similar in purpose to the `DONT_BREAK_ON_ASSERT` setting.

-nobigpicture.help: Start in regular mode (force Big Picture mode off)
-nobigpicture.what: Force the normal desktop UI at startup, overriding a saved Big Picture or gamepad UI startup mode. The client logs "forcing desktopui via -nobigpicture".

-nobootstrapperupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: don't update the bootstrapper binary itself during the update step.

-noconsole.what: Steam UI flag: hide or disable the developer console. It is the opposite of `-console`.

-nocrashdialog.what: tier0/crash-handler flag: don't show a crash dialog when a Steam process crashes.

-nocrashmonitor.what: steamclient.so flag: don't start the crash-monitor process that watches the client.

-nodircheck.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the install-directory checks, e.g. non-ASCII path and writability (`.writable`).

-nodpiscale.what: VGUI flag: disable DPI scaling of the legacy VGUI UI, overriding the `DPIScaling` registry setting.

-nofriendsui.what: Don't load the friends UI module (friendsui.so). The friends list and chat are then unavailable.

-noipv6.what: steamclient.so flag: disable IPv6 networking and use only IPv4.

-nojoy.what: Disable controller support in steamclient and in the streaming client: no SDL/HID controller enumeration, no Steam Input.

-nojsreload.what: Steam UI flag: don't reload the Steam UI JavaScript when it changes, probably a developer hot-reload setting.

-nopcshutdown.what: Steam UI switch: skip real PC power operations (shutdown/restart/suspend) when they are triggered from the UI, so testing Big Picture power menus doesn't power off the machine.

-norepairfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip repairing files that fail verification ("Skipping file repair").

-noshaders.what: Disable the shader pre-caching manager (no shader cache downloads/uploads or Fossilize background processing).

-noverifyfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip verifying client files at startup ("Verification skipped").

-offlinemode.help: Always attempt to start in offline mode
-offlinemode.what: Always try to start Steam in offline mode, using cached credentials.

-openalldevtools.help: Open Chrome devtools on launch for every HTML window
-openalldevtools.what: Open a Chrome DevTools window at launch for every HTML window: Steam UI, overlay (gamepad/desktop overlay) and friends.

-opendevtools.help: Open Chrome devtools for shared JS context (offscreen window) on launch
-opendevtools.what: Open Chrome DevTools at launch for the shared JS context, the offscreen SharedJSContext browser that hosts most Steam UI logic.

-opengl.help: Use the OpenGL render for the UI
-opengl.what: Legacy VGUI switch: use the OpenGL renderer for the UI.

-openoverlaydevtools.help: Open Chrome devtools on creation of any overlay browsers
-openoverlaydevtools.what: Open Chrome DevTools automatically whenever an in-game overlay browser is created.

-out-file.help: Store the response in a file
-out-file.what: steamsysinfo option `-out-file <path>`: write the query response to a file instead of stdout.

-overlay-gpu-pri-delay.help: Set ms delay between overlay GPU priority changes
-overlay-gpu-pri-delay.what: `-overlay-gpu-pri-delay <ms>`: delay in milliseconds between changes of the webhelper GPU priority as the overlay is shown or hidden.

-overlaylogging.what: Enable logging from the in-game overlay renderer, probably into gameprocess/overlay logs.

-overlaytestmode.help: Forces overlay testmode mode for debugging
-overlaytestmode.what: Force the overlay into its test mode for debugging.

-overrideminos.what: Bootstrapper flag: bypass the minimum-OS-version check. Valve's bootstrapper message documents it: "You may override this check by passing -overrideminos".

-pid.help: Pid that we should be watching for
-pid.what: Internal switch for overlay and HTML helper processes: `-pid <pid>` is the process they watch, i.e. the game the overlay is attached to. The client passes it.

-pipewire.what: Enable PipeWire-based desktop capture, used by Remote Play and recording on Linux.

-pipewire-dmabuf.help: Enable PipeWire desktop capture using DMA-BUF
-pipewire-dmabuf.what: Enable PipeWire desktop capture with DMA-BUF zero-copy buffers.

-pipewire-fresh-start.help: Clear all Pipewire capture tokens and re-prompt user for what to capture
-pipewire-fresh-start.what: Clear all saved PipeWire capture tokens, so the user is asked again what to capture (the portal screen-share prompt).

-pipewire-record-deck-ui.help: Record Steam UI elements on SteamDeck
-pipewire-record-deck-ui.what: Include Steam UI elements in PipeWire captures/recordings on Steam Deck.

-pretendeol.what: Steam UI test flag: pretend this OS/platform has reached end of life, to show the EOL warning UI.

-pretendeol32.what: Steam UI test flag: pretend 32-bit support has reached end of life, to show the corresponding warning UI.

-preventsteamdiscovery.what: steamclient.so flag: stop this client from broadcasting or being discovered by other Steam clients on the LAN (Remote Play / In-Home Streaming discovery).

-private_ip_override.what: steamclient.so switch that probably takes an IP address to report as the machine's private/LAN IP, e.g. for streaming or P2P testing. Evidence is only the name.

-profilestartup.what: Profile client startup: record and log startup timing for steamui, steamclient and CEF (e.g. "STARTUP SteamUI browser requested at +%.0fms").

-pyrowavestats.help: Log pyrowave encoding performance to streaming_log.txt
-pyrowavestats.what: Log performance of the pyrowave video encoder (used for Remote Play streaming) to `streaming_log.txt`.

-query.what: steamsysinfo option `-query <command>`: picks which EChildProcessQueryCommand system-info query to run. Steam spawns steamsysinfo as a helper child process.

-query-arg.help: Argument for the query, the meaning depends on the query
-query-arg.what: steamsysinfo option `-query-arg <value>`: the argument for the `-query` command; its meaning depends on the query.

-quicklogin.help: Set the base used to construct quick login URLs
-quicklogin.what: `-quicklogin <base>`: sets the base URL used to build quick-login URLs. A Valve dev option used with `-devsites`.

-rememberpassword.help: If logging in user with credentials specified on the command line, proceed as if 'remember my password' had been enabled
-rememberpassword.what: With `-login <user> <pass>`, act as if 'Remember my password' was ticked, so a refresh token is saved.

-set_locale_disable.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the `setlocale()` call at startup (normally en_US.UTF-8 or the user locale).

-setbeta.what: `-setbeta <branch>`: permanently switch the client to a beta branch by writing it to `package/beta`. The log says "Changing client beta ... (changebeta flag)".

-showallbetas.what: Show all client beta branches in the beta selection UI, not only the filtered list.

-shutdown.what: Tell a running Steam instance to shut down. The command line is forwarded to it and handled by CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine.

-silent.what: Start Steam silently, minimized to the system tray with no main window. The bootstrapper also respects it to keep its update UI quiet.

-simulatedownloaderrors.what: Bootstrapper test hook: simulate package download failures.

-simulatefatalerror.what: Bootstrapper test hook: trigger a fatal error on purpose ("Forcing a fatal error").

-single_core.help: Force Steam to run on your primary CPU only
-single_core.what: Restrict Steam (steamclient and steamservice) to the primary CPU core.

-singleapp.what: Single-app mode (`-singleapp <appid>` is likely): the bootstrapper and UI run Steam as a launcher for one app, reading `launcher\appid` from config/config.vdf and erroring if it is missing. Used for branded launchers, e.g. with `-steamchina`.

-sitelicense.what: steamclient.so flag: run this client as a site-license provider (internet cafe / site license host). It logs "Running as site license provider"; a convar can enable the same.

-skipinitialbootstrap.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the first-run bootstrap step.

-skipstreamingdrivers.what: Remote Play switch: skip the streaming driver checks (virtual audio/input drivers) before starting a stream.

-skipsystemcheck.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip system-compatibility checks, e.g. the steam-runtime requirements check and GL renderer checks such as the VirtualBox 3D-acceleration warning.

-sls-skip-version-check.help: Don't validate the SLS version before starting
-sls-skip-version-check.what: Steam UI switch: don't validate the SLS version before starting. SLS is probably Steam Link Service or a similar component; exact meaning unknown.

-srt-logger-opened.what: Internal flag added by steam.sh / the bootstrapper after it opens the srt-logger (writing `logs/console-linux.txt`), so the logger isn't opened twice, including after an exit-code-42 restart.

-stack=.what: tier0 switch, probably `-stack=<size>`, setting the stack size for the main/worker threads. No usage strings.

-steamchina.what: Bootstrapper flag: run as the Steam China (Perfect World) client, with China-specific packages and universe; often used with `-singleapp`.

-steamconsole.what: Steam UI flag, probably loading `steamconsole.so` or a standalone console mode. It appears next to the survey/`-hometest` code, so the exact effect is unclear.

-steamdeck.what: tier0 platform flag: run the client as if on a Steam Deck (enables Deck-specific UI and behavior). Commonly used with `-gamepadui` to emulate a Deck on desktop.

-steamdeckdisplay.what: Make the client (UI, CEF, overlay) assume a Steam Deck display/panel profile. It is read by almost every component and is probably used for Deck emulation.

-steamframe.what: tier0 platform flag for the Steam Frame hardware (related to the `-deckard` codename). It makes the client behave as on that device.

-steamid.what: steamsysinfo option `-steamid <id>`: the Steam user identifier attached to reports.

-steaminstaller.what: Steam UI command-line verb, probably used by the Steam installer to hand off to the client after installation. Exact behavior unknown.

-steammachinedisplay.what: Like `-steamdeckdisplay`, but makes the client assume a Steam Machine (TV/living-room) display profile.

-steamos.what: Bootstrapper and steam.sh flag: run as SteamOS. steam.sh sets `STEAMOS=1` and skips the 32-bit library check; the client enables SteamOS behavior.

-steamos3.what: SteamOS 3 (holo/jupiter, i.e. Steam Deck OS) platform flag, read by steam.sh and tier0. Equivalent to `-holo`.

-steampid.what: Internal gameoverlayui switch: `-steampid <pid>`, the PID of the Steam process that launched the overlay.

-system-composer.help: Force the use of the system browser composer
-system-composer.what: Steam UI switch: force the system browser composer (compositing path) for Big Picture rather than Steam's own composer.

-tenfoot.help: Start in Steam Big Picture mode
-tenfoot.what: Start in Big Picture mode. This is the historical name and an alias of `-bigpicture`; the startup logic may promote it to the gamepad UI.

-tesla.what: tier0 platform flag named after hardware codename Tesla. Effect unknown.

-testled.what: Create a fake LED device to test the client's LED control features.

-testlongoobeupdater.what: steamclient system-manager test flag: use a slow dummy updater during the OOBE ("applying dummy update", progress posts), to test the long update flow.

-testoobe.what: Force the out-of-box experience flow (sets/reads `ForceOOBE`) in client, UI and CEF. Used for testing first-run setup.

-testoobeupdater.help: Use a dummy updater during oobe
-testoobeupdater.what: Use a dummy updater during the OOBE, so the system-update step can be tested without a real update.

-testssa.what: Force the Steam Subscriber Agreement (SSA) acceptance dialog to show.

-teststoragedata.what: Steam UI test switch: show fake ('test') storage data, probably in the Storage Manager / storage settings page, so the UI can be tested without real drives.

-testupdater.what: steamclient system-manager test flag: probably uses a test/dummy system updater (the SteamOS update path) instead of the real one. It sits near the battery/fan/suspend system-manager code.

-textclient.what: Bootstrapper flag: use the text/console update UI (CConsoleUpdateUI) instead of the graphical update window, e.g. for headless runs.

-toggle-overlay-html-mode.help: Disables new faster overlay HTML path (or enables if on a branch it's not on by default for)
-toggle-overlay-html-mode.what: Flip the default of the new, faster overlay HTML rendering path: it turns the path off where it is on by default, and on in branches where it isn't yet the default.

-uninstall.what: Steam UI command-line verb: uninstall an app, probably `-uninstall <appid>`. It is forwarded to the running client (CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine).

-use_xcomposite_workaround.what: steamwebhelper flag: capture window textures through the XComposite workaround path ("using xcomposite workaround"). Same as setting `STEAM_ENABLE_XCOMPOSITE_WORKAROUND`; the client sets it automatically for some drivers.

-usepipewireaudio.what: steamclient.so switch: use the PipeWire audio backend (e.g. for voice, Remote Play or recording audio) instead of the default backend.

-userchooser.help: Sends the user to the User Chooser even if they have 0 or 1 accounts
-userchooser.what: Always show the account chooser at login, even with 0 or 1 saved accounts.

-verbose.what: steamclient.so flag found next to the site-license code. It probably makes site-license provider mode log more detail; any wider effect is unknown.

-verbose-computer-activity.what: Log verbosely how the client detects user/computer activity, i.e. idle vs. active (used for away status and idle-time features).

-verbosejslogging.help: enable verbose logging of JS console events
-verbosejslogging.what: steamwebhelper switch: log JS console events verbosely. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-verbose-js-logging`.

-verifyfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: verify the checksums of all client files at startup and repair mismatches ("Verifying all file checksums"). It is also read in steamclient.so. steam.sh tries to add it after a failed runtime unpack, but a script bug means the flag never reaches the client.

-vguifocus.help: Print out details of which panel has keyboard focus
-vguifocus.what: VGUI debug switch: print which panel has keyboard focus. Only affects legacy VGUI panels.

-vguimessages.help: set to see debug vgiui2 messages
-vguimessages.what: VGUI debug switch: print debug output for vgui2 panel messages.

-voicerelay.what: Testing switch: allow voice chat only through relay connections, with no direct P2P.

-vrdisable.help: Disable VR - never even try to load OpenVR DLLs
-vrdisable.what: Disable SteamVR integration completely: Steam never loads the OpenVR libraries.

-vrforce.help: Always perform Hmd status check even if we crashed the last time we tried
-vrforce.what: Always run the HMD (headset) status check at startup, even if it crashed last time. By default a crash disables the check.

-vrlinkforceenable.help: Force-enable VR Link capability for testing regardless of platform/encoder
-vrlinkforceenable.what: Testing switch: report VR Link (streaming VR to a headset) as available regardless of platform or video encoder.

-vronly.what: Legacy Steam UI switch, probably a VR-only startup mode with no desktop UI. It is registered next to the old `-opengl` UI renderer switches.

-vrskip.help: Skip VR initialization entirely no matter who asks for it
-vrskip.what: Skip VR initialization entirely, no matter which component asks for it.

-websocket.help: forces connection to Steam backend to be via WebSocket
-websocket.what: Connect to the Steam backend (CM servers) over WebSocket instead of TCP/UDP. Can help behind restrictive firewalls or proxies.

-websocketignorecertissues.help: says it's ok to ignore cert validation issues if using WebSocket connections, for dev use only
-websocketignorecertissues.what: With `-websocket`, ignore TLS certificate validation errors on the WebSocket CM connection. Valve marks it as for dev use only.

-windowed.what: Run Big Picture in a window instead of fullscreen. The bootstrapper also reads it to choose a windowed update UI.
